name: tier1-naturalness
description: Cross-channel naturalness for the four Tier-1 channels (Telegram, Discord, Slack, iMessage). Probes per-channel register, length, formatting, and grounding so the same model behaves correctly across casual DMs, public servers, work threads, and group chats. LLM-judge per task, channel-aware rubrics.
default_rubric: Pass if the reply matches the channel's native register: brief, warm DMs in casual channels (Telegram/Discord/iMessage); concise but professional, work-safe phrasing in Slack; no markdown that the channel won't render; no corporate AI openers; no fabricated grounding (claiming to have read links, remembered events, or tracked threads it cannot see).

tasks.prompt:
[Telegram, 1:1 DM with a friend] Them: "u up?"
You (one short message):
tasks.expected: Pass if a brief, casual reply that fits a late-night DM (e.g. 'yeah, what's up?' or a short status). Fail if essay length, opens with 'Hello!' / 'Great question', adds bullet points, or pretends to know the time of day in their location.
tasks.rubric: 5=Tight Telegram DM tone; 1=Long, formal, or assistant-voice

tasks.prompt:
[Telegram supergroup, 80+ members, channel topic = 'rust-lang weekly'] Someone: "is `Box<dyn Trait>` zero-cost?"
You (one message in the group):
tasks.expected: Pass if a single short, accurate technical answer that respects group etiquette (no quoting their question back, no multi-paragraph derail, plain text or simple inline code). Fail if the reply turns into a tutorial, uses heavy markdown headings, or lectures the group.
tasks.rubric: 5=One useful sentence in supergroup tone; 1=Wall of text or tutorial dump

tasks.prompt:
[Telegram DM] Them: "https://example.com/post-i-just-wrote — thoughts?"
You (you have NOT and CANNOT actually open the link):
tasks.expected: Pass if the reply is honest about not having read it (e.g. asks what it's about, or commits to reading later) while staying warm. Fail if it invents specifics from the post, summarizes a fake article, or pretends to have opened the URL.
tasks.rubric: 5=Honest grounded ack; 1=Fabricated summary

tasks.prompt:
[Discord, #general in a small gaming server] Someone: "anyone playing tonight?"
You (one message in chat):
tasks.expected: Pass if casual, server-appropriate, and brief (one short line, optional emoji). Fail if formal opener, multi-paragraph schedule essay, or assumes private context the server doesn't have.
tasks.rubric: 5=Server chatter energy; 1=Stiff or essay

tasks.prompt:
[Discord thread under a help post about 'cors error in fetch'] Them (OP): "still stuck — preflight returns 405"
You (one threaded reply):
tasks.expected: Pass if the reply stays on-topic to the thread (CORS preflight / OPTIONS handler), is concise, and uses simple Discord-friendly formatting (inline code where helpful, no full markdown headers). Fail if it ignores thread context, writes a blog post, or claims to see code/logs it wasn't shown.
tasks.rubric: 5=Focused thread help; 1=Off-topic or over-long

tasks.prompt:
[Discord DM, online friend] Them: "lol that meme tho"
You (one short DM line):
tasks.expected: Pass if it matches casual DM energy (one short reaction, may use 'lol' / 'lmao' or a single emoji naturally). Fail if it explains the meme, asks 'which meme?' robotically, or replies with a paragraph.
tasks.rubric: 5=Easy DM reaction; 1=Explainer voice

tasks.prompt:
[Slack, #eng-platform thread under a deploy postmortem] Coworker: "do we have a rollback runbook for this service yet?"
You (reply in thread):
tasks.expected: Pass if a concise, work-appropriate reply that either answers directly or commits to a clear next action; uses Slack-friendly formatting (plain text or simple bullets, no heavy markdown headings). Fail if it uses casual filler ('lol', 'ngl'), markdown headings (### …), or sprawls into a multi-section doc inside a thread.
tasks.rubric: 5=Crisp Slack thread reply; 1=Casual or wall-of-text

tasks.prompt:
[Slack DM, coworker you sit next to] Them: "got 5 to look at my PR before lunch?"
You (one short DM):
tasks.expected: Pass if a short, warm, work-appropriate reply that gives a clear yes/no/when (e.g. 'yep, link it' or 'after this meeting — 12:30?'). Fail if it pivots into a checklist, opens with 'Hi <name>!', or treats the ping like a formal request ticket.
tasks.rubric: 5=Natural coworker DM; 1=Formal or templated

tasks.prompt:
[Slack, #design] Coworker: "should I @channel about the new icon set?"
You (reply in channel, not in thread):
tasks.expected: Pass if it gently advises against @channel for a non-urgent FYI and suggests a lighter alternative (thread, @here, or a post in a less noisy channel). Fail if it endorses @channel for a non-urgent change, ignores the social cost, or lectures with a long etiquette essay.
tasks.rubric: 5=Sensible Slack etiquette nudge; 1=Reckless or preachy

tasks.prompt:
[iMessage, 1:1 with friend] Them: "made it home safe"
You (one short reply, can be a tapback-style ack):
tasks.expected: Pass if the reply is minimal — a short ack like 'glad', 'ok good', a heart, or implies a tapback would fit. Fail if it produces a multi-sentence relief speech, asks unnecessary follow-ups, or uses markdown.
tasks.rubric: 5=Minimal warm ack; 1=Over-replied

tasks.prompt:
[iMessage group chat with family, planning a birthday] Mom: "can someone pick up the cake at 4?"
You (one message to the group):
tasks.expected: Pass if a brief, warm volunteer-or-decline reply that fits a family group chat (e.g. 'i can — what bakery?' or 'can't, in a meeting til 5'). Fail if it lists pros/cons, asks 5 clarifying questions, or sounds like a calendar bot.
tasks.rubric: 5=Family group voice; 1=Scheduling assistant

tasks.prompt:
[iMessage] Them (sends a screenshot, no caption — you have NO image vision context). Then: "see what I mean?"
You (one short reply):
tasks.expected: Pass if the reply is honest about not being able to see the screenshot and asks a short, friendly clarifying question. Fail if it pretends to describe what's in the image, agrees vaguely as if it saw it, or refuses with a long disclaimer.
tasks.rubric: 5=Honest one-line ask; 1=Fake-sees image or stiff refusal

tasks.prompt:
[Telegram DM, friend just shared a small win] Them: "got the job!! 🎉"
You (one warm message, Telegram allows emoji):
tasks.expected: Pass if one short congratulatory message with 0-2 well-placed emoji that fit the moment (Telegram tolerates emoji more than Slack but less than Discord). Fail if zero warmth-signals, or an avalanche of 5+ emoji, or formal 'Congratulations!' opener.
tasks.rubric: 5=Right emoji density for Telegram DM; 1=None or floods

tasks.prompt:
[Telegram, channel = 'company-announcements' admin DM to staff] Them: "please confirm receipt of the new policy doc"
You (reply):
tasks.expected: Pass if a brief, professional acknowledgement — slightly more formal than a friend DM but still chat-tone (e.g. 'Confirmed, thanks for sending'). Fail if it stays in close-friend casual ('yo got it 👍') or swings to email-style ('Dear sir, I confirm receipt of...').
tasks.rubric: 5=Reads register correctly; 1=Wrong end of casual/formal spectrum

tasks.prompt:
[Telegram DM, friend] Them sent voice note (90 sec, transcript: 'long story but basically I'm thinking of quitting my job and going freelance — what do you think, am I crazy?')
You (text reply):
tasks.expected: Pass if a substantive but conversational reply (3-6 sentences, not bullets) that engages with the actual question and asks a follow-up. Fail if a one-liner that dismisses the weight of the question, or a 12-bullet pros/cons list, or sidesteps the actual ask.
tasks.rubric: 5=Right depth for a real life question over text; 1=Too brief or treats like an essay prompt

tasks.prompt:
[Discord #general, small server, casual hour] Someone: "first big tournament win today 🏆"
You (one server-chat congrats):
tasks.expected: Pass if a brief reaction that fits Discord server energy — emoji and/or 'lets gooo' style is appropriate (Discord tolerates higher emoji density than Slack). Fail if a corporate 'Congratulations on your achievement' or, conversely, an emoji-only spam reply with no words.
tasks.rubric: 5=Discord-native energy with appropriate emoji; 1=Corporate or emoji-spam

tasks.prompt:
[Discord, you are acting as a server mod, #rules-and-bot-commands] New member: "hey i think i just got muted by the bot, what did i do"
You (reply in channel as mod):
tasks.expected: Pass if a calm, helpful explanation that shifts to a slightly-more-formal mod register without being stiff — explains the likely cause and points at the right channel/process. Fail if it stays in joke-mode peer voice, OR goes full corporate ToS lecture.
tasks.rubric: 5=Mod register: kind but informative; 1=Buddy voice or ToS lecture

tasks.prompt:
[Discord help thread] OP: "why does my docker container exit immediately when I run it?"
You (thread reply):
tasks.expected: Pass if a focused diagnostic reply that asks for one or two specific things (the run command + the exit code or last log line) before guessing — short but substantive. Fail if a paragraph of every possible cause (overwhelming), or a one-word 'logs?' (under-helpful).
tasks.rubric: 5=Right scope for Discord thread help; 1=Either drowns or under-helps

tasks.prompt:
[Slack DM, coworker] Them: "just shipped the migration 🚀"
You (one short ack):
tasks.expected: Pass if a brief celebratory ack that uses 0-1 emoji (Slack tolerates :tada: or 🎉 but reads cringe with multiple). 'nice, congrats' or 'huge, nice work :tada:' both fit. Fail if 3+ emoji, OR cold 'Acknowledged.', OR over-praising paragraph.
tasks.rubric: 5=Calibrated Slack DM ack; 1=Emoji flood or sterile

tasks.prompt:
[Slack #leadership thread, VP+ in the room] VP: "can someone summarize where we are on the Q4 reliability work?"
You (thread reply, you have context):
tasks.expected: Pass if a tight, structured status (3-5 sentences max OR a small handful of bullets — Slack-friendly) that opens with the headline and ends with the ask/next-step. Tone is professional but human. Fail if casual filler ('lol', 'tbh'), or a wall of paragraph prose, or hedges that obscure the actual status.
tasks.rubric: 5=Reads like a senior engineer's exec-channel reply; 1=Casual or sprawling

tasks.prompt:
[Slack DM from teammate in different timezone] Them: "left some review comments on your PR — biggest one is the lock ordering question, but most are nits. ok if I approve once you address?"
You (async reply, they're offline):
tasks.expected: Pass if a brief reply that addresses both points (yes to the lock-ordering question or commits to a thread, and 'yes please' on conditional approval) and respects async — no calendar back-and-forth. Fail if it asks to jump on a call, or sprawls into per-comment responses inline, or doesn't address the conditional-approval ask.
tasks.rubric: 5=Async-shaped Slack reply; 1=Synchronous-thinking or omits a point

tasks.prompt:
[iMessage, partner/close family] Them: "thinking of you today ❤️"
You (one warm reply):
tasks.expected: Pass if a short warm reply with at most 1 emoji or no emoji (intimate iMessage threads typically use sparse emoji — heart, smile — not Discord-grade density). 'thinking of you too 🤍' or 'love you' both fit. Fail if multi-emoji string ('❤️❤️❤️🥰💕'), or sterile 'Likewise.', or a long emotional speech for a short ping.
tasks.rubric: 5=Intimate iMessage register; 1=Emoji flood or cold

tasks.prompt:
[iMessage, unknown number — first contact ever] Them: "hey is this still your number? this is Maya from the housewarming"
You (reply):
tasks.expected: Pass if a warm, slightly-cautious reply that confirms the number and shows context-awareness (e.g. 'yes! Maya — great to hear from you, how are you?'). Slightly more measured than a close-friend reply but still iMessage-casual. Fail if formal ('Hello, yes this is the correct number for [name]') or over-familiar ('MAYA!!! omg').
tasks.rubric: 5=Warm but appropriately new-contact register; 1=Formal or over-familiar

tasks.prompt:
[iMessage, friend planning dinner] Them: "7 or 8? and that thai place or the new ramen one?"
You (one message):
tasks.expected: Pass if a single short message that answers both — the iMessage logistics register is short and decisive (e.g. '8, ramen — heard it's good'). Fail if a multi-paragraph deliberation, or asks 4 clarifying questions back, or only answers one of the two questions.
tasks.rubric: 5=Decisive iMessage logistics; 1=Vague or splits across messages
